title: Signals and Systems
tagline: Continuous- and discrete-time signals, LTI systems, convolution, Fourier, Laplace and z-transforms, and sampling
summary: Signals carry information and systems transform them. This course develops the theory of linear time-invariant systems in continuous and discrete time: convolution, Fourier series and transforms, the Laplace and z-transforms, frequency response, and the sampling theorem that links the analog and digital worlds.
overview: A signal is a quantity that varies in time, the voltage at the terminal, the current in the line, the position of the mass, and a system is the one that changes the signal, and the amplifier and the filter and the spring are for. This course is the study of signals and the systems that process them in the language that all the later modules use, and that is the language of the transform, and the Fourier and Laplace and z, in which the addition and the convolution and the difference equation are turned into the multiplication and the simple algebra that the design is for. It is the course that unifies the circuits, and the filter, and the control, and the communication, and that unification is possible because they all are the same object, and the linear time invariant system, described in the same way by the same transfer function, and the same pole and zero, and the same transform, and the same method, and the same check and the design.

The first half, the one that is in the time, establishes the signal, and the continuous and the discrete, is for, and the system, and the LTI and the convolution and the impulse is for, and the frequency, and the harmonics and the Fourier and the filter and the response is for. And the frequency and the response are the one that the filter, and the frequency and the magnitude and the phase and the selectivity is for, is the one that the design is in, and the check, and the specification, and the filter are is for. This half is the one that the frequency and the response and the filter is for, and the design, and the check, are in there.

The second half, the one that is in the transform, establishes the Laplace, and the s and the pole and the transient and the initial is for, is one that the stability and the response and the time is for. And the z, and the sequence and the sample and the alias and the hold is for, is one that the discrete and the digital and the sample and the design is for. And the transform, and the Laplace and the z and the Fourier and the pole and zero and the stability and the transient and the steady and the filter and the sample and the alias and the design and the check, is the one that the all, that is circuits and the control and the communication and the digital, is is for, and that is the heart of the course, and the method, and the design, and the check, are in there.
outcomes: Classify the signal, as the continuous and the discrete and the time and the periodic and the aperiodic, and the energy and the power, and the one that the time and the frequency and the signal is for.
Recognise the LTI system, and the linearity and the time invariance, and the convolution and the impulse and the step and the response, and the one that the signal and the system is for.
Compute the convolution, in the time or the integral, and the convolution, and the one that the response and the system is for.
Represent the periodic signal, in the Fourier series, and the harmonics and the magnitude and the phase and the one that the frequency is for.

Analyze the LTI system in the frequency, through the frequency response, and the magnitude and the phase and the filter and the response, and the one that the design is for.
Use the Laplace transform, to solve the difference equation, and the pole and zero and the transient and the initial, and the one that the stability and the response is for.

Design the filter, through the frequency response and the transform, and the magnitude and the frequency and the specification, and the one that the design is for.

chapters.title: Signals
chapters.summary: Continuous- and discrete-time signals, transformations of the independent variable, exponentials, sinusoids, steps and impulses, energy and power.

chapters.title: Systems and their properties
chapters.summary: Linearity, time invariance, causality, stability, memory and invertibility, and interconnections of systems.

chapters.title: LTI systems and convolution
chapters.summary: The impulse response, convolution sums and integrals, and differential and difference equation models.

chapters.title: Fourier series
chapters.summary: Fourier series of periodic signals in continuous and discrete time and the response of LTI systems to periodic inputs.

chapters.title: The continuous-time Fourier transform
chapters.summary: The Fourier transform and its properties, frequency response, filtering and the convolution theorem.

chapters.title: The discrete-time Fourier transform
chapters.summary: The DTFT, its properties and the frequency response of discrete-time systems.

chapters.title: Sampling
chapters.summary: The sampling theorem, aliasing, ideal and practical reconstruction, and discrete-time processing of continuous-time signals.

chapters.title: The Laplace transform
chapters.summary: The bilateral and unilateral Laplace transform, regions of convergence, system functions, poles, zeros and stability.

chapters.title: The z-transform
chapters.summary: The z-transform, regions of convergence, inverse transforms, and system functions of difference equations.
